I'm not writing to sell you equipment. I'm writing because I see an interesting synergy between our companies across the Middle East market. OUR CUSTOMERS OVERLAP — AND THAT'S AN OPPORTUNITY FOR BOTH OF US. We understand Panatek is a well-established supplier of SMT, THT, and PCB manufacturing equipment, covering the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, and the broader Middle East region. Your ability to deliver complete turnkey solutions to electronics manufacturers in this market is exactly the kind of capability we value. Here's the logic: ● When a PCB manufacturer invests in new wet process equipment (electroless copper, plating lines, ENIG), they almost always need SMT and assembly equipment as well — which is your domain. ● Conversely, when one of your customers expands their SMT and assembly capacity, they often think about upgrading their upstream PCB fabrication capabilities — which is where Commend comes in. WHAT I'M PROPOSING: ● We can keep each other informed about relevant developments in the Middle East PCB and electronics manufacturing market — under strict confidentiality, of course. ● If one of our customers signals a need for SMT or assembly equipment, we can recommend Panatek. If one of your customers is thinking about new PCB wet process equipment, we would greatly appreciate a recommendation our way. ● Together, we could offer customers a more complete package: Commend's wet process expertise + Panatek's SMT and assembly solutions. I would be delighted if we could have a brief, no-obligation phone or video call — 15 minutes would be enough to see whether a cooperation makes sense for both sides. 131808.desc: Dear Sir and Madam, We are pleased to share with you Paulownia's innovative insights on replacing pine wood products in architectural exterior wall panels. The innovative paulownia wood cladding will help you to enter the wood construction market. It is a new source of revenue growth. Central China International Resources Corp. has FSC Certificate, is one of Chinese corporations, who has been exporting wood products for more than 20 years. Pine wood is widely used as a building exterior cladding material in European and American markets. Based on the functional characteristics of solid wood panels on the exterior facade, CCIRC compares the technical parameters of paulownia wood and pine wood in the air dry density, ignition point, thermal conductivity, thermal resistance, moisture barrier performance, natural resistance to decay, mildew and weather resistance. The conclusions are as follows: Paulownia wood building materials are more suitable for exterior cladding wall panel, wood curtain wall, laths, garden furniture, fencing components,decorative fencing. Paulownia wood is a preferred choice for wooden decoration materials in dry environments, areas prone to fire exposure (as outdoor barbecues, cigarette butt disposal), and densely populated zones (as shopping malls, schools, hospitals). CCIRC looks forward to co-operate with you to explore Paulownia exterior cladding wood products, share market needs, and benefit for both you and we. The attachment of comparison: Paulownia’ Core Physical Parameters Excels Pine wood as below. As a natural lightweight wood, Paulownia wood features straight and clearly visible grain, with a soft natural light yellow color. The distinction between heartwood and sapwood is not obvious. The thermal treated paulownia wood building materials have better performance than the natural paulownia wood products. End of Voyage Declaration (EOV) An End of Voyage Declaration is when a shipping line officially declares that the vessel will not continue to its originally scheduled destination ports because the voyage cannot be safely completed. This usually happens due to: War or military conflict, Closure of sea routes, Blocked ports ,Security risks to vessel and crew, Government restrictions, Insurance restrictions (War Risk insurance) In such cases, the carrier may decide to: Stop the voyage at a safe port, Discharge containers at an alternative port, Suspend further sailing toward the intended port The voyage officially ends there, and cargo will be discharged. All extra costs are usually charged to cargo owners.

133127.title: DO/Booking status Held in Sent - Middleware Manual Intervention Required
133127.desc: We are receiving a high volume of complaints from multiple shipping lines regarding Delivery Order (DO) and Booking updates that remain stuck in “Sent” status within the system. These transactions are not progressing automatically as expected and instead require manual intervention from the Middleware team to complete processing. Preliminary observations indicate that the messages are successfully generated by the shipping lines but are not being acknowledged or processed by the Middleware layer. This results in the status remaining in “Sent” without moving to the next stage (Processed/Completed). The issue appears to be recurring and affects operational efficiency, customer satisfaction, and SLA commitments with shipping lines. Reference case ID: 133115 and previous known cases.

133257.title: DO Validity Update Failing Due to Terminal Rejection - Quantity Mismatch in API Payload
133257.desc: Reference case ID: 133256 and existing known issues. When the shipping line updates the DO validity and sends the updated DO to the terminal, the CMATK rejects the update with the following error on Empty return terminal status. ERRKEY_QTY_LESSER_THAN_ASSOCIATED_UNITS: Quantity 0 is lesser than the number of associated units 1 with this item. The shipping line’s DO update payload is being sent with Quantity = 0, even though the DO has 1 associated container. CMATK TOS enforces strict validation and rejects the update because the quantity in the payload does not match the number of associated units. As a result, ATLP does not receive the updated validity and continues to display the previous expiry date. Current Workaround (Temporary Solution): We (biztalk) are manually updating DO validity in ATLP and request the CMA terminal to update in their TOS as well. Request you to review and prevent repeated failures, and eliminate the need for manual intervention.

133298.desc: Refer ticket# 130045 We would like to raise a system enhancement request regarding a recurring issue in the EPASS SYSTEM Currently, when a user submits gate pass request and selects an Area to Visit, if the request is returned by the gate pass Officer for modification or correction, the system does not allow the user to edit the selected Area to Visit field. As a result, users are required to contact our team to manually update the area on their behalf. In accordance with Administrative Resolution No. (69) of 2025 issued by the Chairman of the Department of Municipalities and Transport (DMT) concerning the Regulatory Bylaw for Maritime Safety in the Waterways of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, entities undertaking maritime activities within the Emirate are required to obtain the applicable permits, approvals, and No Objection Certificates issued by Abu Dhabi Maritime on behalf of DMT. 133595.title: Streamlining the Land PTW Activation  Contract Mapping Workflow in ATLP

h.v: CancelledNotes: Not valid for the problem, it

133595.desc: Problem Statement The current Land PTW activation process requires multiple manual steps involving email communication, form exchanges, and coordination between ATLP Support, PTW Office, and the Senyar Team. This results in: 1. Delays in contract activation 2. Lack of visibility on request status 3. Repeated follow‑ups by users 4. High dependency on manual intervention 5. Increased processing time for contractors 6. Frequent user confusion regarding prerequisites These inefficiencies directly impact operational timelines, especially for contractors who require urgent PTW access to begin on‑site activities. Current Workflow START │ ▼ 1. Company & User Registration in ATLP │ ▼ 2. User sends email to PTW Office / support@atlp.ae requesting PTW activation │ ▼ 3. ATLP/PTW Office sends Contract Activation Form - UCID - Contract Number - Company Details - Contact Information │ ▼ 4. PTW Office assists user to fill contract details │ ▼ 5. Senyar Team verifies & creates/updates contract │ ▼ 6. ATLP Team maps Senyar Contract to Company UCID │ ▼ 7. ATLP grants Senyar Access to the Company │ ▼ 8. User can now submit Land PTW Request │ ▼ END Key Pain Points 1. No unified workflow inside ATLP 2. Users must rely on email communication 3. No automated validation of UCID, contract, or access 4. No real‑time status tracking 5. Multiple teams involved without system‑driven coordination 6. High manual workload for PTW Office and ATLP Support 7. Delays in PTW activation affecting project timelines Proposed Solution A fully integrated, automated Land PTW Activation Module inside ATLP START │ ▼ 1. User selects “Land PTW Activation Request” in ATLP │ ▼ 2. System auto-validates: - UCID status - Company registration - Trade license validity │ ▼ 3. User enters Contract Number │ ▼ 4. System checks Senyar Database: - If contract exists → Auto-map to UCID - If contract missing → Auto-create request to Senyar Team │ ▼ 5. Real-time status tracking visible to user: - Contract verification - Mapping progress - Access provisioning │ ▼ 6. System automatically grants PTW access once mapping is complete │ ▼ 7. User can immediately submit Land PTW Request │ ▼ END Expected Benefits For Users 1. Faster PTW activation 2. No need for email follow‑ups 3. Clear visibility of request status 4. Reduced confusion and errors For PTW Office / ATLP Support 1. Reduced manual workload 2. Fewer email requests 3. Automated contract mapping Improved accuracy and processing speed For ATLP 1. Stronger user experience 2. Higher system adoption 3. Reduced operational bottlenecks 4. Better data consistency across ATLP & Senyar Request We kindly request the ATLP Product Team to evaluate and implement the proposed enhancement to streamline the Land PTW activation process, reduce manual dependencies, and improve overall operational efficiency for contractors and internal teams. Evidence Attached sample emails for your reference.

134692.title: External Notification
134692.desc: Dear KEZAD Contact / Free Zone Authority Team, We are Next Gen Alternative Nicotine Manufacturing Ltd, currently establishing a manufacturing facility in KEZAD. We are evaluating the conditions for our company to qualify as a "Qualifying Free Zone Person" (QFZP) to benefit from the 0% Corporate Tax rate on Qualifying Income. As per Federal Decree-Law No. 47 of 2022 (Article 18) and Cabinet Decision No. 55 of 2023 (Article 4 — Adequate Economic Substance Requirements), a QFZP must, among other requirements, "maintain an adequate number of full-time qualified employees (or equivalent) in the UAE to undertake its Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA)." We understand from the FTA Free Zone Persons Guide (CTGFZP1) that the economic substance test is qualitative and assessed on a case-by-case basis, rather than being tied to a fixed headcount. To ensure our setup is compliant from the outset, we would greatly appreciate KEZAD's guidance on the following points: 1. **Regarding "Adequate Number" of Employees:** For a pure manufacturing operation, does KEZAD provide any indicative benchmarks, expectations, or internal practices concerning the number and type of full-time staff (e.g., operators, supervisors, QA, planners) required to be considered as having "adequate economic substance"? Or is this assessment solely conducted by the FTA without KEZAD's direct involvement? 2. **Employees Hired Through an Employer of Record (EOR) / Outsourced Manpower Supplier:** A significant portion of our workforce will be engaged through outsourced manpower or labor-supply arrangements. In such cases, the employees' labor cards and visas are held by the manpower supplier, not directly by our KEZAD entity. Could KEZAD please advise: * Whether these outsourced/seconded employees, who work full-time at our KEZAD facility, can be counted towards the "adequate number of full-time qualified employees" requirement for QFZP purposes. * Whether KEZAD has any preference or requirement for core production personnel to hold labor cards and visas issued directly under the KEZAD entity. 3. **Physical Presence vs. Remote Work:** Must all qualifying employees be physically based and work within the KEZAD free zone? Or can certain roles (e.g., support functions) be performed remotely while still contributing to the economic substance requirement? We aim to ensure that our staffing structure and visa/labor card arrangements are correctly established to maintain our QFZP eligibility. Any guidance you can provide, or a referral to the appropriate FTA contact if these questions fall outside KEZAD's scope, would be highly valued.

134748.title: Request for Urgent Resolution of Duplicate Certificate Issue
134748.desc: We are facing a recurring issue while updating vessel certificates in the system. In most cases, after uploading a renewed certificate and submitting it to the Harbour Master, the application is placed on Hold due to duplicate certificates. Before uploading the renewed certificate, we always delete the expired certificate from the system. However, the expired certificate is still visible to the Harbour Master, causing the system to display both the expired and the updated certificates. We own and manage more than 80 vessels, and our fleet operates continuously within the UAE, calling at ports, offshore bases, and private jetties on a daily basis. The repeated hold status delays vessel approvals, disrupts our operations, and has resulted in complaints from our clients. Expected Result: Once an expired certificate is deleted from the system, it should no longer be visible to the Harbour Master. Only the latest valid certificate should be displayed for review to avoid duplicate certificate issues and unnecessary hold status. We kindly request your urgent support in investigating and resolving this issue, as it is significantly affecting our day-to-day vessel operations.

Currently, after renomination is completed, the shipment details are not visible to the user until the agent logs in and manually accepts the renomination request. Only after this step is completed can the user proceed to view the shipment, declare customs, and create the required appointments. This dependency is causing delays for users, as they are required to continuously follow up with the ATLP team for acceptance. This is particularly critical for air shipments , where timely processing is essential due to their urgent and time-sensitive nature. Impact: Delay in customs declaration Delay in appointment creation Increased dependency on manual intervention Frequent follow-ups from users Request: We kindly request a system enhancement to enable automatic acceptance of renomination requests , especially for air shipments. Your support in reviewing this request and implementing a suitable solution is highly appreciated. Thank you for your continuous support.

135106.title: ATLP Appointment Search Error Missing BL Numbers
135106.desc: Problem / Issue Statement In the ATLP SEA Appointment System, users intermittently experience issues when attempting to search for appointments using Bill of Lading (BL) numbers. The problem does not occur consistently but affects specific cases. Root cause: Investigation shows that the root cause is missing values in the BillOfLadingNumber field within the database table mgappt.TruckVisitAppointmentContainers for DI transactions. Because the BL number is not always stored in this field, the system is unable to retrieve the corresponding appointments during search operations, resulting in incomplete or failed search results for affected users. Second issue: After applying the data fix and searching by Bill of Lading (BL) number on the ATLP SEA Appointment screen, appointment records do not appear on the first search attempt. However, when the user performs the same search again, the records successfully appear.

135122.title: Users are uploading large files, up to 27MB, which is causing performance issues in the mLMS application
135122.desc: Issue: Users are uploading large files, up to 27MB, which is causing performance issues in the mLMS application, particularly in the truck operator and road tanker operator license modules. Root Cause: The mLMS application is not optimized to handle large file uploads efficiently. The current system architecture and resource allocation are insufficient to manage the high data load, leading to slow response times and potential system crashes. Solution: Implement File Size Restrictions: Limit the maximum file size that can be uploaded to the application to a more manageable size, such as 1 or 2 MB. Optimize File Handling: Enhance the application's backend to better manage large file uploads, including implementing file compression and efficient data processing techniques. User Education: Provide guidelines and training for users on how to reduce file sizes before uploading, such as using file compression tools

135129.title: Users with mobile numbers registered outside the UAE are not receiving OTP numbers on the ATLP portal.

Network or carrier restrictions in the user's country might be blocking the OTP messages. Solution: Verify if the OTP service provider supports international SMS delivery. If not, consider switching to a provider that does. Check and update the ATLP portal configuration to ensure it supports sending OTPs to international numbers. Communicate with the network carriers to ensure there are no restrictions on receiving international SMS.

While my family is doing their best to care for him, no one can replace a mother’s presence, comfort, and support—especially for a child with such critical needs. I sincerely and respectfully request your compassion and understanding of my situation. Your support in expediting the issuance of my Visa and EID would allow me to return home to my children, especially my son, who urgently needs me. Your kindness and prompt assistance would mean more to my family than words can express. I will remain deeply grateful for your understanding and support during this difficult time.

Workaround: Update the status to provisional approved with the appointment number 2607010295 So we can cancel the appointment from ATLP, and the same will be cancelled from the terminal TOS. The error comes from the CSP terminal, but the issue scenario is the same for all terminals. This occurs when users delete an appointment in ATLP, but the deletion does not sync to the terminal’s TOS. As a result, the terminal continues to read the old appointment as active, causing new appointments for the same container to be rejected. Expected action: deleted in ATLP but still alive in terminal TOS Stale (deleted in ATLP but still alive in terminal TOS) appointment numbers to be removed or cancelled from terminal TOS while user deleting an appointment.

Here is a breakdown of what it means: The Issue: The shipping container bearing the identification number SEGU3215763 is currently throwing a system error (likely in a Terminal Operating System or a shipping line's software). The system does not currently recognize this container as being eligible for the "import cycle." This usually happens if the container is mistakenly registered under a different status (such as an export, an empty return, or already gated out). The Container Number (SEGU3215763): * SEG: The owner/operator prefix (typically identifying the shipping line or leasing company). U: Denotes that it is a freight container. 321576: The unique 6-digit serial number. 3: The check digit used to verify the accuracy of the previous numbers. The Action Required: The sender is requesting a system administrator, terminal operator, or shipping agent to manually override or update the container's status in their database. Changing it to the "import cycle" will clear the error, allowing the container to be legally discharged from a vessel, cleared through customs, and released for delivery to the consignee.

The Action Required: The sender is instructing a shipping agent, terminal coordinator, or operations team to intervene. They need to identify why the terminal rejected the document (e.g., missing customs clearance, unpaid terminal handling charges, or a system glitch) and take the necessary steps to have the terminal "accept" and validate the Delivery Order.

136402.desc: Issue Description: The Booking Bulk Upload process is currently failing for Fujairah Terminal bookings because the system validates the voyage customs status and customs booking number provided in the upload template. However, customs declarations are not applicable for Fujairah Terminal voyages, causing the validation to fail and preventing successful bulk uploads. Proposed Solution: Modify the Booking Bulk Upload process to exclude customs status and customs booking number validations for Fujairah Terminal voyages, allowing bookings to be uploaded successfully without customs declaration-related checks.

Your guidance on the applicable requirements and recommended approach would be greatly appreciated.

136577.title: ATLP Booking Validation Failure – System Allows Multiple Active ACP Bookings for Same Container
136577.desc: Reference case: 136572 ATLP allows users to create multiple bookings for the same container, even when an existing booking is already in ACP (Accepted) status at the terminal. For container IGIU9252153, the system currently shows: Two MTY‑OUT bookings already accepted by ADT One MTY‑IN booking created in advance and also accepted Because ATLP does not validate or block duplicate ACP bookings, the container ends up with multiple active booking flows (Empty Out + Empty In simultaneously). This causes the system to fail during appointment creation and results in the error: “No containers found.” The system is unable to determine the correct flow due to conflicting active bookings, leading to operational delays and manual intervention from terminal and support teams.

csat.scenario: owner resolved own ticket ON TIME

136585.desc: Dear Team, Greetings, It has been noticed that we are receiving weight mismatches in FAO bookings. It appears that the weight received from the agent through the booking differs from the weight reflected in the COPARN, where the container tare weight seems to have been added to the declared cargo weight. Example: * Agent's declared gross weight for a 40' container: 29,000 kg (include tare weight) * Weight received in COPARN: 32,840 kg. This results in a discrepancy of 3,840 kg, which appears to be the container tare weight. Kindly investigate and resolve this issue at the earliest to avoid container shout-outs, as many containers are being received with weights exceeding their CSC plate limits due to this discrepancy. If the issue is caused by incorrect weight declarations or booking submissions from the agents' side, we kindly request that appropriate training and guidance be arranged for all shipping agents to ensure FAO bookings are uploaded with the correct gross weight. This will help prevent future discrepancies and avoid operational delays. Your prompt attention and support in resolving this matter will be highly appreciated. Thanks Kashif Nawaz Yard PlannerPorts

137452.title: EDI Distribution for New Stack Codes (OOC1, COS1 & ONE1)
137452.desc: Please be informed that we have recently added additional stack codes for OOCL, COSCO, and ONE as OOC1, COS1, and ONE1. Means, these lines will now have two stack codes (e.g., OOC and OOC1). These additional stack codes have been created purely for terminal operational convenience, as the containers under each stack are managed differently, although they belong to the same shipping line. And terminal is sending EDI files (COARRI, CODECO, etc.) using the operator code exactly as maintained in the terminal system. Therefore, any movement of containers under the OOC stack are sent with operator code OOC, while those under the OOC1 stack are sent with operator code OOC1. Looks like the EDI files containing these new operator codes (COS1, OOC1 & ONE1) are not being distributed to the respective shipping lines from your side. Could you please verify whether these files are being forwarded to the customers? If not, we kindly request that MG to do the required mapping - so that OOC1, COS1, and ONE1 EDI files are delivered to the correct shipping lines. Appreciate your support here. Attached email fyr. Further, we may be requesting a new code for MAERSK line - MSK1 soon. Waiting for some internal confirmation.

137501.title: Duplicate FAO/COPARN acceptance in Terminal system

csat.scenario: owner off shift, BREACHED (covering shift — collective)

137501.desc: Dear ATLP Team, Greetings. It has been noticed that agents are creating FAO bookings, which are successfully received by the terminal. Subsequently, the same container details are being resent to the terminal under a different booking number, POD, and operator, and these messages are also being accepted by the system. This issue should be handled as follows: 1. Duplicate FAO Submission * If an FAO has already been successfully received for a container, any subsequent submission of the same container under a new booking should be rejected by the system. * An appropriate error message should be generated indicating a duplicate container record. 2. FAO Amendment Submission * If the agent intends to modify an existing booking, the updated information should be sent as an amendment message. * In such cases, the terminal system should maintain only one active COPARN record for the container. * The EDI retains details of both the original and amended messages for reference purposes. Kindly investigate this issue as a matter of urgency and implement the necessary corrective action at the earliest to avoid any incorrect acceptance of bookings in the terminal system, which may lead to operational discrepancies. Your prompt attention and support on this matter will be highly appreciated. Please find the below email for your reference. Thanks Kashif Nawaz Yard PlannerPorts

137968.title: Clarification Regarding Customs Codes, HS Codes, and VAT Registration for International Shipping
137968.desc: Hello, I would like to ask for clarification regarding international shipping from the UAE. I have a free zone company license and I am planning to ship products internationally. However, I have also spoken with a courier company, and they advised that they only require HS codes for the products being shipped. I have found two HS codes on your website that appear to match the products I intend to export. Could you please clarify whether there is a difference between customs codes and HS codes? Additionally, is VAT registration required in order to ship internationally from the UAE? I would appreciate your guidance on the requirements and any steps I need to complete.

138174.title: Exklusive China-Europa-Raten mit wisecargo logistics
138174.desc: Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren, ich hoffe, diese Nachricht erreicht Sie gut. mein Name ist Mahomes von Right Freight. Wir sind ein international tätiges Speditionsunternehmen mit langjähriger Erfahrung im Bereich der China–Europa-Verkehre. Als Mitglied der internationalen Netzwerke WCA und Lognet verfügen wir über mehr als 20 Jahre Erfahrung in der globalen Logistik. Unser Schwerpunkt liegt auf Seefracht, Luftfracht und Bahntransporten zwischen China und Europa. Zudem bieten wir komplette Exportlösungen inklusive FCL/LCL-Abwicklung, Vorlauf, Verzollung sowie maßgeschneiderte Logistiklösungen an. Gerne möchten wir Ihnen unsere aktuellen Sonder-Seefrachtraten von China nach Europa anbieten: China → North West Europe (NWE) POL: Qingdao / Shanghai / Ningbo / Xiamen / Yantian POD: Rotterdam / Hamburg / Wilhelmshaven / Le Havre / Antwerpen / Southampton / Felixstowe / Algeciras Ocean Freight:USD 2,750 / 4,300 / 4,300 -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- China → Mediterranean (MED Ports) POL: Qingdao / Shanghai / Ningbo / Xiamen / Yantian POD: Barcelona / Valencia / Genoa / Fos / La Spezia / Algeciras Ocean Freight:USD 3,300 / 5,200 / 5,200 Validity: Until 31 July Sollten Sie weitere Relationen, spezielle Anforderungen oder individuelle Transportlösungen benötigen, erstellen wir Ihnen gerne ein entsprechendes Angebot. Wir freuen uns auf Ihre Anfragen und auf die Möglichkeit einer langfristigen erfolgreichen Zusammenarbeit. Mit freundlichen Grüßen Mahomes Right Freight
